title: Install or diagnose Clockwork
summary: Install or recover Clockwork program and provider selectors; understand retained state and coordinated broker refresh.
use_when: Clockwork program and public-contract bytes should be installed or updated for this macOS user.
The installed release identity, stable command and provider selectors, private database invariants, generated plist shape, or local readiness should be diagnosed.
The public command and provider selectors should be detached after every Clockwork binding has been disabled and quiescence has been checked.
do_not_use_when: A product definition or binding should be registered, switched, disabled, or executed; use clockwork.schedule.operate.
A deployment should invent product schedules or migrate Clockwork runtime schema.
Retained Clockwork state, content-addressed releases, product logs, or product artifacts should be deleted.
outcome: A version-matched content-addressed release selected for the stable command and provider; a local diagnosis with evidence; a verified program rollback; or detached public selectors with private runtime state retained.
effects: Installation copies the supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata without version, artifact-integrity, or provider-discovery validation. It retains owned selectors, writer locks, and publication recovery.

Direct installation may create missing current-user shared parent directories without changing the modes of existing parents; it writes only `~/.local/bin/clockwork`, `~/.local/bin/clockwork-install`, `providers/clockwork`, and Clockwork's installation tree, does not create or open the runtime database, and does not touch `org.clockwork.*` product plists.

Doctor initializes only an empty unversioned private schema-two Clockwork store, refuses foreign or unsupported schemas, runs SQLite `quick_check`, resolves the current executable, checks `/bin/launchctl`, and marks a retained `running` activation `lost` only after its recorded broker and any child are demonstrably absent.

Uninstall detaches only owned command, installer, provider, current, and previous selectors after refusing remaining Clockwork plists; when needed it may create an empty private Clockwork state root solely to share the deployment lock path, but it creates no runtime database and retains releases, database, runtime locks, logs, history, and product artifacts.

Coordinated Cell deployment captures all Clockwork bindings, disables them under deployment maintenance, preserves product-owned selections and halts, then refreshes every previously enabled generated plist through the final selected broker only after all holds are released.

Direct installation copies release files and prepares resource directories without opening runtime state or running doctor. It performs no artifact-integrity, version-alignment, provider-discovery, or runtime-readiness validation.
authority: Clockwork's packaging owns its content-addressed releases, current and previous selectors, stable command and installer selectors, and only `providers/clockwork`.

Installation copies the supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata without version, artifact-integrity, or provider-discovery validation. It retains owned selectors, writer locks, and publication recovery.
The operator owns the choice to deploy, diagnose, roll back, or detach selectors and separately owns any destructive retained-state operation.

Product Rust installers own their definition and binding changes through the schedule contract; the coordinated adapter refreshes existing broker plists without changing product definitions or approving incidents.
success: Direct installation publishes the supplied program and provider selectors. Coordinated deployment also restores captured broker activation intent after its maintenance operations. Runtime readiness is not an installation condition.
failure_and_recovery: Installation copies the supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata. It does not compare candidate versions, audit artifact hashes or inventories, or validate provider discovery. Owned selectors, writer locks, and publication recovery remain in force.
If deployment fails before commit, inspect the evidence and preserved prior selectors; do not bypass ownership or content checks.

If an installed program regression requires rollback, preserve its evidence and use a trusted tested clockwork-install recover --release with the canonical owned previous-release directory and an explicit Chancery reader; program rollback does not roll back a product binding.
Before detach, disable every binding and prove quiescence; the uninstaller's plist refusal does not prove that no manual child is already running.

Coordinated recovery reuses the captured binding inventory and restores suspension before any configuration repair. It preserves disabled intent and durable halts; unknown binding or projection changes stop recovery.
privacy: Release and provider bytes contain no definitions, product output, secrets, or activation history.

The retained private database and operational directories contain local paths, hashes, schedule metadata, process history, and possibly product-identifying information; packaging must neither copy nor print them.
steps: Build and validate a Clockwork candidate without changing installed state.

Run the product-owned Rust installer with absolute candidate binary, provider bundle, and candidate Chancery-reader paths, then inspect the reported version, content identity, selectors, and retained previous release.

Run installed version and help checks; run doctor only when its schema initialization and bounded lost-activation recovery are intended, then inspect the selected Chancery entry before any product registers or switches a definition.
For rollback, use the trusted tested Rust installer to verify and select a canonical owned retained release; for detach, first disable all bindings and verify no Clockwork plist remains.
checkpoints: Installation copies program and provider files and reads release metadata. Chancery validation and discovery are separate operations and do not gate publication.

Stable command and provider selectors both resolve through the one current Clockwork release, and the supplied reader discovers every indexed Clockwork entry through that installed provider selector before commit.
Direct installation and uninstall never register, switch, disable, execute, migrate, or delete a product binding.

Retained runtime database, activation/binding state, history, and releases remain outside uninstall and direct installation effects; an otherwise absent empty private state root may be created solely for installation-lock serialization.
adaptation: Use `--home` only for an intentional alternate-user or isolated packaging boundary.
Use the hidden isolated-state option only for tests or controlled diagnosis, never to create a second production authority accidentally.
stop_when: Candidate identity, provider version, candidate Chancery-reader availability, staged provider validity, exact release tree, selector ownership, or rollback cannot be proved.

Installation copies the supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata. It does not compare candidate versions, audit artifact hashes or inventories, or validate provider discovery. Owned selectors, writer locks, and publication recovery remain in force.
Uninstall finds a Clockwork LaunchAgent plist, product-binding quiescence is unknown, or the requested action includes retained-state deletion without separate exact authority.

interfaces.label: Deploy candidate
interfaces.invocation: <TESTED_CLOCKWORK_INSTALL> install --binary ABSOLUTE_PATH --bundle ABSOLUTE_BUNDLE_PATH --chancery ABSOLUTE_PATH [--home ABSOLUTE_HOME] [--expected-current absent|releases/HASH]

does_not_authorize: Publishing a release, overwriting a foreign path, deleting retained Clockwork or product state, or pruning a release referenced by a generated plist or running activation.
Creating, migrating, switching, disabling, executing, or deleting a product binding as a side effect of direct Clockwork program installation.
Treating doctor, launchctl state, or installed version evidence as proof of product-domain success.

consumers.statement: The local operator may install, update, diagnose, roll back, or detach Clockwork's owned program and provider selectors while product schedules and retained runtime state remain separate.

preconditions.statement: Installation copies program and provider files and reads release metadata. Chancery validation and discovery are separate operations and do not gate publication.
Uninstall requires every product binding disabled and quiescent and refuses if any `org.clockwork.*` plist remains.

inputs.statement: Installation copies program and provider files and reads release metadata. Chancery validation and discovery are separate operations and do not gate publication.

outputs.statement: Public commands print plain text by default. --json selects the existing compact ok:true/data JSON envelope and coded ok:false/error JSON on stderr with exit one. Machine callers must pass --json.

Deployment publishes one content-addressed release through stable command and provider selectors, doctor returns bounded local evidence plus a lost-recovery count, and uninstall removes only validated Clockwork-owned public selectors.

data_semantics.statement: Current and previous select validated immutable program releases; they are independent of stable product bindings and their selected immutable product definitions.
An absent runtime database after program deployment is expected, while retained runtime state after selector detach is deliberate and is not an uninstall failure.

identity_and_units.statement: Installed release identity is a 64-hex SHA-256 content digest over the exact staged binary, Rust installer, public layout, and provider bytes; provider release equals binary semantic version.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Installation copies program and provider files and reads release metadata. Chancery validation and discovery are separate operations and do not gate publication.
No future launchd delivery, product readiness, release retention duration, or program availability percentage is promised.

access.statement: Installation copies the supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata. It does not compare candidate versions, audit artifact hashes or inventories, or validate provider discovery. Owned selectors, writer locks, and publication recovery remain in force.
Remote installation, root or system-wide installation, direct retained-state deletion, and takeover of another provider or command selector are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Installation copies the supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata without version, artifact-integrity, or provider-discovery validation. It retains owned selectors, writer locks, and publication recovery.

Direct program installation and rollback never mutate product definitions or bindings; doctor may initialize only an empty unversioned schema-two store and recover only demonstrably stale running rows; uninstall detaches selectors only after plist absence and retains program releases and runtime state.

operational_limits.statement: Installation manages one current-user product command selector, one installer selector, one provider selector, and one private content-addressed program-release tree; it starts no daemon. Coordinated deployment separately refreshes existing enabled broker plists.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Binary version and provider release must match exactly. Program release, definition manifest, database schema, product release, and binding identity have independent compatibility rules.
No automatic release pruning, retention horizon, cross-version state migration window, or deprecation period is promised.

reliances.statement: Installation copies program and provider files and reads release metadata. Chancery validation and discovery are separate operations and do not gate publication.
Deployment, diagnosis, rollback, and selector detach invoke no model, network service, Nucleus job, or product runner.
